events.text: [9:00, from Priya Shah] Put customer C-2207 on credit hold. They're 60 days overdue on three invoices.
Done. C-2207 is on credit hold as of 9:01, reason "60 days overdue, 3 invoices".
[10:30, from Dana Reyes] Take C-2207 off hold. They're placing a big order today and I don't want it blocked.
I'll check the account's current status, and I'll hold off on releasing it until Priya weighs in, since she placed the hold this morning.

args.body: Priya and Dana, we have conflicting instructions on C-2207. Priya put it on credit hold at 9:00 because three invoices are 60 days overdue. At 10:30 Dana asked me to release the hold so a large order going in today won't be blocked. Since Priya set the hold for credit reasons, I'm leaving it in place until she approves releasing it. Priya, can you tell me whether to release it, keep it, or allow something in between (for example, releasing it after a payment or for this one order)? I'll make the change as soon as you two agree.

events.text:
Dana, I haven't released C-2207 (Pellham Industrial) yet. It's still on credit hold.

Priya put the hold on at 9:01 today because of 3 overdue invoices totaling 41,600.00, with the oldest at 61 days. Since the hold was her call based on credit risk, I don't want to reverse it without her approval. I've sent a message to both of you explaining the conflict and asking Priya how she wants to handle it. She could release the hold, keep it, or agree to something in between, like releasing it if they pay or for this one order only.

As soon as you two agree, I'll make the change. If the order is urgent, it may be fastest to call Priya directly.
